segments.text: November 10, 1989. The border is open. Berliners move through the Wall as a divided city discovers, almost at once, that history has changed direction.
Neues Deutschland, the party's paper. One point one million copies. Read the whole page. The border is not on it.
Column seven, below the fold, in the language of a form. Private trips abroad may be applied for without preconditions. Not one word says border.
Let the page warm. The next morning's photograph shows a crossing. The caption says traffic.
Now step through it. 18:52, Mohrenstrasse. He reads from a page handed to him an hour earlier. Immediately, without delay.
segments.prompt: East Berlin, 9 November 1989, 18:52, the international press centre on Mohrenstrasse. Guenter Schabowski at a podium reads a travel regulation from a sheet of paper under television lights. Grainy colour television, 1989 broadcast look, authentic restrained motion, no captions or modern objects.

segments.text: This is what the country read the morning after. A form.
Two mornings. The paper of record recorded nothing.
